name: fraud_claim
description: Pay or hold a customer's fraud claim
subject: user
hold: Should the pending fraud claim be held for manual review, and not paid automatically, because it shows signs that the customer made or authorised the disputed transactions, or signs of claim abuse?

typologies.third_party_fraud: Genuine unauthorised use: a criminal used the card details or took over the account
typologies.scam_victim: Scam victim: the customer made the payment personally because someone deceived them
typologies.first_party_fraud: First-party fraud: the customer made the transactions and disputes them to get the money back
typologies.claim_abuse: Claim abuse: a pattern of repeated claims, or claims coordinated with other customers

reasons.usual_device_or_location: The disputed transactions came from the customer's usual device, IP address or home city
reasons.known_merchant_or_payee: The customer paid the same merchant or payee before without a dispute
reasons.late_claim: The claim was filed weeks after the disputed transactions with no explanation
reasons.prior_claims: The customer filed other fraud claims in the past year
reasons.prior_abuse_or_red_flag: The customer has a confirmed red flag or an earlier claim closed as account abuse
reasons.linked_to_abusers: The device or the payee is shared with other customers who have account-abuse outcomes
reasons.takeover_signs: A new device, a password reset or a contact change came shortly before the disputed transactions
reasons.merchant_or_payee_reported: The merchant or the payee carries a fraud, scam or mule-account report
reasons.card_testing: Small test payments came before larger ones at a merchant the customer never used
reasons.customer_authorised: The claim description says that the customer made or approved the payment personally
